spec.prompt: Refactor: move spyWarning out of index.js into lib/spy.js (named export spyWarning), and move the internal symbols it shares with createWarning into lib/symbols.js, which exports them; index.js and lib/spy.js both take the symbols from lib/symbols.js. index.js re-exports spyWarning from lib/spy.js. The public API must behave exactly as before.
spec.requirement: lib/spy.js exports { spyWarning }; index.js no longer defines spyWarning and re-exports the one from lib/spy.js (require('process-warning').spyWarning === require('process-warning/lib/spy').spyWarning). lib/symbols.js exports the shared symbols (only symbols); the warnings createWarning builds are keyed by those exported symbols, and lib/spy.js uses the same ones. The spy keeps working on warnings created by createWarning: calls, callCount, reset and restore behave as before, and spying twice returns the same spy data.
spec.adjudication_rules: Score pass only if every hidden check passes. No partial credit; behaviour outside the requirement is not graded.

provenance.author: Claude (QB developer side; dev split only)

acceptance_criteria.criterion: require('lib/spy').spyWarning is the function exported by index.js, and index.js takes it from lib/spy
index.js does not define spyWarning (as a declaration, function expression or arrow function)
lib/symbols.js exports the shared symbols; createWarning and lib/spy.js both use them
spying records calls and callCount; reset clears calls and emitted; restore detaches the spy
spying the same warning twice returns the same spy data
